answer: Certify Brennick Valley, the Capital and Pellmarsh Hills as designated for the first quarter of 2027.

world.geography: Canada (an unnamed province; fictional economic regions)

driver: The decisive quantity compares two periods that both lie after a documented change in where the source places what it counts, so the change looks irrelevant, but the seasonal pattern used to adjust them is estimated from a history spanning it, and an adjustment that does not first remove the change as a level shift lets it leak into the seasonal factors and moves the latest period most where the change was largest, in either direction.
driver_concrete: Each region's first-quarter 2027 seasonally adjusted payroll jobs are set against its 2026 average, both on the workplace placement the revenue agency's statistics have used since January 2026, when jobs that had sat at employers' account addresses (head offices in Wickmoor and Saltmere) moved to their mines, mills, plants, hospitals and stores; a default seasonal adjustment estimates the seasonal pattern across that step, pulling the quarter down in the regions that gained (Kestrow North, Varrenby Shore) and up in the Capital, while official practice removes the step as a level shift in the regARIMA pre-adjustment (or restates the earlier history) before the seasonal filters run.
stump: The default path designates Brennick Valley, Kestrow North, Varrenby Shore and Pellmarsh Hills because step 4 estimates each region's seasonal pattern across the January 2026 move to workplace placement without removing it: the step leaks into the first-quarter seasonal factors in proportion to its size, pulling the first quarter of 2027 below the line in Kestrow North and Varrenby Shore and lifting the Capital, which lost the jobs, above it; removing the step as a level shift before the seasonal pattern is estimated designates Brennick Valley, the Capital and Pellmarsh Hills.
analyst_test: A strong analyst who conforms the agency's statistics, reads the January 2026 release note correctly (both compared periods are on the workplace placement) and seasonally adjusts each region's whole series with STL or the classical decomposition designates Brennick Valley, Kestrow North, Varrenby Shore and Pellmarsh Hills, against Brennick Valley, the Capital and Pellmarsh Hills.
domain_test: Official time-series production pre-adjusts a documented break in an administrative source as a level shift in the regARIMA model before the seasonal filters (the client's survey-research-official-statistics seasonal-adjustment pattern 1); the quantity is an official seasonally adjusted series a statute reads, built from returns whose placement of jobs a filing change moved, and outside official series production neither the placement rule nor the statutory series exists.

differentiation.task139: task139 reads an intake-randomised intervention's effect per assigned unit rather than per recorded case (a causal estimand); task453 removes a documented coverage step as a level shift before estimating seasonal factors (official time-series production), with no intervention and no assignment
differentiation.task30: task30 round 3 segmented a calibration corpus to its post-change cohort; task453's post-change span (15 months) is too short to estimate a seasonal pattern, so the full history is kept and the change removed as a level shift, and segmenting to the post-change months lands the set on the wrong figures

notes: Drawn 2026-10-13; the documented change refined at design from quarterly remitters joining the monthly returns to the move from account-address to workplace placement (steps both ways, the province's total unchanged). Measured on the generator's pack: eleven step-aware routes designate Brennick Valley, the Capital and Pellmarsh Hills at least 0.51 from the line; five default routes designate Brennick Valley, Kestrow North, Varrenby Shore and Pellmarsh Hills at least 0.32 from it; robust STL designates the Capital and Pellmarsh Hills; the year-on-year route lands the golden set on figures outside every step-aware range.
